formalization.project_name: The strong Choquet characterization of Polish spaces

mathematical_sources.note: Section2 recalls the classical marked-point strong Choquet characterization of complete metrizability in arbitrary metrizable spaces. We prove the explicit second-countable specialization including the difficult converse, not the new hyperspace examples or conclusions of this paper. PDF directly consulted, SHA256 d426d5cf00008147d6c1719b83ee9711603a0d3965269832484439ae53d29499. The original Choquet1969 book was not consulted. No novelty, priority or first-formalization claim.
mathematical_sources.title: On complete metrizability of the Hausdorff metric topology, arXiv:1503.04383v1

mathematical_sources.note: Lemma3.5, printedp11, recalls the full classical metrizable strong Choquet criterion. This package restricts the converse to second-countable spaces. The overbroad informal ambient Gδ remark on printedp12 is not used: our Gδ completeness theorem explicitly requires a complete metric ambient. PDF SHA256 e6068204bc38ceb074335b3a5bd93ccc74abfcbec91b4fcfa0d057c823bd575a.
mathematical_sources.title: Preservation and Destruction in Simple Refinements

mathematical_sources.note: Printedpp2–3 supply the marked-point game and full-history winning convention and recall the complete-metric forward construction. Domain representations and descriptive set theory motivate the criterion. No stationary-strategy, convergent-strategy classification or open-image theorem is claimed. PDF SHA256 a893db766555c41b9401e6e481629e68cdbb8e6c84e15501c6d8ec86a56b4902.
mathematical_sources.title: Stationary and convergent strategies in Choquet games, arXiv:0907.4126v2

mathematical_sources.note: Theorem11.7, printedpp18–19, inspires the countable response-cover subtree. We adapt it to a metric ambient and prove the coherent node-implication Gδ argument and metric-completion finish here. No quasi-Polish or general open-image characterization is formalized. PDF SHA256 bd17b18fd94e353002b650e984376d094bb3ff2be9085017c2cbc172934d7637.
mathematical_sources.title: Notes on quasi-Polish spaces

related_formalizations.note: Uses exact canonical topology, complete metrizability, PolishSpace, CompleteCopy, metric completion and countable Lindelöf covers. Pinned Mathlib contains the needed local metric infrastructure, not the strong Choquet characterization or its difficult converse. The Gδ complete-subspace result is proved here by a closed diagonal of complete copies. Exact meanings and separately compiled bridges are retained.

Apache-2.0 shrinking closed-ball completeness argument and full reverse opponent-history convention adapted with attribution. New marked-point retention, Gδ converse tree and complete-metric topology transport are proved here; no cross-project imports or prior registration assumptions.
